propositions: A TOCTOU race in transition_close.py allows HEAD to move between verify_completion(ref="HEAD") and the sign step, causing the ticket to close without a completion signature while the verify and sign operations reference different commits.

When HEAD drifts between verify and sign, the close transition proceeds and closes the ticket anyway, leaving it in a permanent unsigned state with no retryable recovery path (re-close is a no-op for already-closed tickets).
The suggested recovery message 'Re-close to certify' is ineffective for closed-but-unsigned tickets; only --force-close or manual manifest fabrication are available as workarounds.
The default code path (no --ref argument) reads HEAD twice independently, splitting verify and sign; only the explicit --ref path pins a single revision coherently across both operations.

A benign race where an unrelated concurrent commit lands between verify and sign should not invalidate a completion attestation for a revision that was successfully verified, per the same principle as the plan-review gate's handling of unrelated drift.
